question: Automated traffic management systems for trains are currently only used on a small section of Europe's railway network. Signalling, remote control systems, ETCS and GSMR contribute to the safer functioning of the railway network. Despite this, only 14% of European rail has an operational automatic train stop system. In view of this: 1.

Is the Commission looking into the possibility of making automatic train stop systems compulsory in EU Member States and, if so, as of when will this apply?
2.
Is it considering other mandatory measures for the safer use of European trains?
answer: The safety level of the EU railway system remains high. In a multi-modal comparison rail appears the safest mode of land transport in the EU (1). Nevertheless, the EU is looking to maintain high safety levels, while harmonising further rail safety requirements EU-wide and introduce efficient, modern systems as soon as they become available.

A wide range of EU technical specifications and EU common safety methods are designed to regulate safe rail operations. As regards train control-command and signalling systems, the European Rail Traffic Management System (ERTMS) will replace existing national ‘class B’ train protection systems, creating a harmonised single European rail area.

The 2024 TEN-T (trans-European transport network) Regulation (2) requires the phasing out of national protection systems and their replacement with ERTMS: Member States must equip their core, extended core and comprehensive networks with ERTMS by 2030, 2040 and 2050, respectively.

Directly applicable Technical Specifications for Interoperability (TSIs) (3), for example in the TSI on control-command and signalling systems (CCS TSI), requires (4) the installation of ERTMS trackside whenever national train protection systems are replaced on any rail line in the EU.

Equipping lines that are not part of the TEN-T network — typically those with lower volumes of traffic may therefore take longer than 2050, depending on the robustness of the train protection systems deployed.

A further obligation is that TSI requires accordingly that new designs of trains or freight locomotives must be equipped with ERTMS onboard, or existing vehicles must be retrofitted when ERTMS trackside is roll-out and national signalling systems are disconnected.
